label: Rest Blocked by Ongoing Signals
coreConflictTemplate: The room is still signaling that something is ongoing, so rest never fully takes over.
topLeverageTemplate: Reduce the strongest unfinished signal nearest the sleep zone.
notYet: Do not start by styling the room.
Do not buy decor before the rest zone is protected.
Do not reorganize the whole room tonight.
likelyFirstRelief: The room may feel less unfinished.
It may be easier to slow down once you get into bed.
The room may feel more like the end of the day.

label: Rest Blocked by an Unprotected Bed Zone
coreConflictTemplate: The bed is present, but it is not being protected strongly enough as a rest-only zone.
topLeverageTemplate: Give the bed its single purpose back before changing anything broader.
notYet: Do not focus on the whole room before the bed feels protected.
Do not add new objects before the bed zone is simplified.
likelyFirstRelief: The room may feel less mixed-purpose.
The bed may read more clearly as a place to stop.
Your mind may feel slightly less busy at bedtime.

label: Calm Blocked by Visual Density
coreConflictTemplate: The eye is being asked to process too much, so the room cannot fully settle the nervous system.
topLeverageTemplate: Reduce the densest visual surface before changing the whole room.
notYet: Do not add decor to a surface that still feels overloaded.
Do not widen the project before one high-pressure surface is reduced.
likelyFirstRelief: The room may feel easier to look at.
The space may start to feel quieter without changing much else.

label: Focus Blocked by Functional Blur
coreConflictTemplate: The space is asking the brain to switch roles too often, so focus never fully locks in.
topLeverageTemplate: Strengthen one clear work anchor before improving the rest of the room.
notYet: Do not optimize ambiance before the work anchor is clear.
Do not spread tools across multiple weak zones.
likelyFirstRelief: The room may feel more directional.
It may be easier to start one task without drifting.
The space may feel less split between modes.

label: Recovery Blocked by Harsh Light Rhythm
coreConflictTemplate: The room does not shift its light rhythm clearly enough, so the body stays more alert than the goal requires.
topLeverageTemplate: Lower and soften the dominant evening light before doing anything decorative.
notYet: Do not start with styling if the room still feels overlit at night.
Do not rely on one bright ceiling source to do every job.
likelyFirstRelief: The room may feel less sharp.
The transition into evening may feel more obvious.
Your body may find it easier to slow down.

label: Safety Blocked by Unheld Space
coreConflictTemplate: The room may be clean and quiet, but it is not holding the body with enough softness or anchor.
topLeverageTemplate: Build one stronger point of support before trying to make the whole room feel warmer.
notYet: Do not add many small accents before the room has one clear anchor.
Do not confuse emptiness with calm.
likelyFirstRelief: The room may feel less exposed.
It may feel easier to stay in the space without hovering.
The space may start to feel more settled.
